impact: County says data was removed from government systems; scope not determined.
date_note: Unusual network activity found on the evening of Monday 16 November; the county confirmed the incident on 17 November (ABC News 4, published 18 November).
title: Charleston County, South Carolina, says data was removed from its systems in a cyber incident
summary: Charleston County, South Carolina, says data was removed from its government systems in a cybersecurity incident, confirmed on 17 November after IT staff saw unusual network activity. Per WCSC, SLED is now treating it as a criminal investigation, and the county calls it a sophisticated cyberattack. Operations and life-safety services continue normally; the county has not said whether residents' data was affected. No actor is named.
plain: A South Carolina county says data was taken from its systems. It has not yet said whether residents' personal details are involved.
exec: Data was removed from a local government’s systems; scope unknown, services running.
action: Residents: change passwords on county-linked accounts, watch bank statements and be wary of messages claiming to be from the county.

key_findings: County says data was removed from government systems; confirmed 17 November.
Unusual network activity found Monday evening 16 November; SLED assisting.
Scope, data types and numbers not determined.

validation.note: Two local outlets (WCIV, WCSC) relay the county statement; the county own notice was not read.

review.note: Checked against ABC News 4: dates, data removed, SLED, no actor match; exec said data theft, stronger than removed, reworded
